description: An endowment needs capital. An annual award needs only a cheque and a school willing to administer it.

title: Start and grow a business
description: Revenue before polish. Most of year one is finding out who actually pays, and what they think they bought.

title: Start something — a business, blog, or side project
description: It doesn't have to succeed. It has to exist.

title: Stay up all night to watch a sunrise
description: On purpose, somewhere beautiful. Tiredness and wonder is a strange combination.

title: Stencil a reusable fabric bag
description: Cut a simple reusable stencil and print a bold design onto an existing tote.

title: Stitch a patchwork cushion cover from scraps
description: Join saved fabric into a usable cushion cover with a deliberate colour arrangement.

title: Stonehenge, England
description: Four thousand years of mystery on a Wiltshire plain. The scale only registers in person.

title: Stretch strudel dough by hand
description: Stretch rested pastry across a cloth-covered table, roll it around a filling and bake it.

title: Submit a complete bird checklist to eBird
description: Record the route, duration and birds from one observation session using the project's checklist rules.

title: Submit a month of rain-gauge observations to a science network
description: Learn the network's equipment and reporting rules, then make a consistent series of observations.

title: Summit a volcano
description: Pick an active or dormant one. The crater at dawn, the sulfur, the scale — nothing else on earth feels quite like it.

title: Support a computer-learning session through a community program
description: Help a learner complete a task they chose while they keep control of their device and accounts.

title: Surf a real wave
description: Not a beginner lesson on the shore break — an actual, rideable wave.

title: Surf a wave over 10 feet
description: Two-storey faces, long hold-downs, and years of smaller water first. Never paddle out on a big day alone.

title: Survive a wilderness expedition
description: Multi-day, self-supported, genuinely remote. The kind where your decisions have consequences.

title: Swim a mile without stopping
description: Roughly 64 lengths of a 25-metre pool. Takes six to twelve weeks of consistent training from a casual swimming base.

title: Swim in all five oceans
description: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, Southern. A slow, deliberate life goal that forces extraordinary travel.

title: Swim in the Dead Sea
description: Ten times saltier than the ocean, so you float without trying. Any cut on your skin will announce itself.

title: Swim with humpback whales
description: Tonga and the Dominican Republic license it. They are the length of a bus and decide how close you get.

title: Take a beginner badminton lesson
description: Learn a comfortable grip and simple court movement, then try a cooperative rally.

title: Take a beginner land-yachting lesson
description: Learn to steer and stop a land yacht with an instructor on an authorized open course.

title: Take a beginner Pilates class
description: Learn the class's basic positions and ask the instructor for suitable adaptations before trying a short sequence.

title: Take a cold plunge every morning for a month
description: Two to three minutes in water under 15 degrees. The shock never stops being shocking, but your recovery gets faster.

title: Take a cooking class in the country the cuisine is from
description: A morning market tour, an afternoon at the stove, and eating what you made. Thailand, Italy, Japan, Vietnam all do this well.

title: Take a forest bathing walk
description: Shinrin-yoku: a slow, sensory walk through a forest. No destination, no pace, no goal except being there.

title: Take a photograph that stops people
description: Not an Instagram shot — something compositionally, emotionally extraordinary.

title: Take a photograph that stops people in their tracks
description: Thousands of frames for the one. Light and timing decide it far more than the camera you own.

title: Take a pottery class and make a finished piece
description: Centring the clay defeats most beginners for several sessions. Expect a third of your pieces to crack in the kiln.

title: Take a road trip with your best friends
description: The long silences in the car are the point. Book less than feels safe and leave afternoons unplanned.

title: Take a sheltered-water paddleboard starter lesson
description: Learn basic control and safe falls with a qualified instructor in conditions selected for beginners.

title: Take a slow travel trip: one town, one week, no plan
description: One small town, seven days, no itinerary. You learn what a place is when you stop trying to see all of it.

title: Take a supervised introductory caving trip
description: Explore a beginner cave route with a qualified provider who supplies appropriate equipment and clear turnaround rules.

title: Take a tea ceremony class
description: A Japanese chakai or a Chinese gongfu session. The ritual is the opposite of efficiency, which is the entire point.

title: Take a trip completely alone
description: One week, solo, somewhere unfamiliar. The most formative thing you can do in your 20s.

title: Take a trip with your parents before it's too late
description: While they're well enough to travel. Go somewhere they've always wanted to go.

title: Take a volunteer call through Be My Eyes
description: Complete the onboarding and assist with a visual task while the caller directs what they want help with.

title: Take an adult beginner swimming lesson
description: Work with a qualified teacher on water confidence and one manageable pool skill.

title: Take an introductory indoor bouldering lesson
description: Learn the gym's landing and downclimbing rules before trying a few low beginner problems.

title: Take part in a seasonal butterfly count
description: Follow an established count's timing and identification rules and submit what you actually observe.

title: Take the Trans-Siberian Railway across Russia
description: Seven days, eight time zones, a samovar at the end of each carriage. Bring food, cards, and low expectations of privacy.

title: Taste chocolate from three origins
description: Compare plain chocolates with declared cacao origins and describe their differences without brand clues.

title: Taste one dish from three local traditions
description: Compare clearly named regional versions of a familiar dish while learning what distinguishes them.

title: Teach a class or course
description: Formally or informally — something you know well, passed on to people who don't yet.

title: Teach a skill you're good at to a group of strangers
description: You will find the holes in your own understanding within ten minutes. Prepare less and demonstrate more.

title: Teach English in a developing country
description: A CELTA takes a month and separates you from volunteers who leave a class worse than they found it.

title: Tell a short story in sand animation
description: Move a shallow layer of sand across a lit surface and perform a sequence of changing images.

title: Tell the most important people in your life why they matter
description: Specific beats general. Name the thing they did and roughly when, not their qualities in the abstract.

title: Temper chocolate and mould a small batch
description: Learn temperature control with chocolate and cast a few glossy bars or shapes.

title: Test a paper glider with controlled design changes
description: Keep a flight log while changing one design feature at a time in a clear indoor space.

title: Test how salt changes a simple dish
description: Prepare one unsalted base and compare measured seasoning levels in tiny portions.

title: The Alhambra, Granada, Spain
description: Islamic palace architecture of extraordinary mathematical precision. The most beautiful building in Europe.

title: The Amalfi Coast, Italy
description: Cliffside villages above turquoise water. The most dramatic coastline in Europe.

title: The Amazon Rainforest, Brazil
description: More species per square kilometre than anywhere else on earth. The lungs of the world, while they still exist.

title: The Atacama Desert, Chile
description: The world's driest non-polar desert — and one of the best places on earth to see the Milky Way.

title: The Camino de Santiago
description: 800km across Spain on foot. The world's most famous pilgrimage — not for religion, but for whatever it teaches you about yourself.

title: The Canadian Rockies
description: Banff, Jasper, Lake Louise — glacier-fed lakes of impossible blue surrounded by peaks that look like set design.

title: The Daintree Rainforest, Australia
description: The world's oldest surviving tropical rainforest, continuously present for 180 million years. Crocodiles in the river, cassowaries in the bush.

title: The Dead Sea, Jordan/Israel
description: Float without swimming. The water is ten times saltier than the ocean. The lowest point on the earth's surface.

title: The Grand Canyon, USA
description: The scale is impossible to understand from photographs. Stand at the rim and look down — a mile of geological time.

title: The Great Barrier Reef, Australia
description: The world's largest coral system — and one of the places changing fastest. Dive it before the bleaching worsens.

title: The Kimberley, Australia
description: Remote wilderness larger than Germany. Ancient Wandjina rock art, gorges, and a coastline no road reaches.

title: The Kimberley coast by boat
description: Accessible only by sea. Horizontal waterfalls, ancient gorges, and Indigenous communities that have lived there for 40,000 years.

title: The Korean DMZ
description: One of the strangest borders on earth — a 4km strip of no-man's land that has become accidentally rewilded.

title: The Norwegian Fjords
description: Glacial water, vertical cliffs, silence. The scale of the landscape makes everything else feel small.

title: The Pyramids of Giza, Egypt
description: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world. Stand at the base of the Great Pyramid and feel the scale of 4,500 years.

title: The Sahara Desert
description: Sleep in a tent in the silence of the world's largest hot desert. Sunrise over dunes with no other human in sight.

title: The Scottish Highlands
description: Moorland, lochs, and castle ruins. Wild in a way that feels pre-historical.

title: The Serengeti, Tanzania
description: The greatest wildlife spectacle on earth. The great migration: two million wildebeest in motion.

title: The Silk Road, Uzbekistan
description: Samarkand, Bukhara, and the turquoise-domed cities of Central Asia. History that most Westerners have never encountered.

title: The Swiss Alps
description: Walk between villages through mountain passes that have been trade routes for two thousand years.

title: The Taj Mahal, India
description: Built as a monument to love. The white marble shifts colour with the light — different at dawn, dusk, and under full moon.

title: The temples of Bagan, Myanmar
description: Two thousand temples across a plain. Balloon at dawn, bicycle at dusk. The most underrated ancient site in Asia.

title: The Whitsunday Islands, Australia
description: 74 tropical islands in the Coral Sea. Whitehaven Beach — almost pure silica — is one of the world's finest.

title: Throw a kiln-fired ceramic pot
description: Wedge, centre, pull, dry slowly, glaze, fire. Six stages, and any one of them can take the piece from you.

title: Throw a party worth remembering
description: Plan it properly. Invite the right mix of people. Make it legendary.

title: Throw a surprise party that genuinely surprises someone
description: One leak ends it. Fewer people in on it, and a cover story boring enough to sound like a Tuesday.

title: Tibet and the Tibetan Plateau
description: The world's highest plateau. Monasteries at 4,000 metres, the Potala Palace, and a sky that looks different at altitude.

title: Trace buildings for a humanitarian mapping task
description: Complete the training and submit a small, carefully reviewed task through an established mapping project.

title: Trace the journey of one inherited object
description: Document what is known, uncertain and private about an object passed between people.

title: Train a small image classifier on your own objects
description: Build a teaching model from household objects and test it against backgrounds it has never seen.

title: Transcribe a historical manuscript for the Smithsonian
description: Help turn a scanned page into searchable text while preserving uncertain readings for review.

title: Translate a free-software resource into a language you know
description: Work with a translation team to make a short, requested piece of documentation usable by more readers.

title: Transylvania, Romania
description: Fortified Saxon villages, medieval towns, and mountain landscapes largely unchanged since the Middle Ages.

title: Trek across Iceland
description: The Laugavegur takes four days. The full north-south crossing takes weeks, over unbridged rivers and grey volcanic sand.

title: Trek to Everest Base Camp
description: Twelve days up, four down, and 5,364 metres doing most of the work on your lungs. Altitude ignores fitness.

title: Try a beginner body scan with a guided recording
description: Follow a brief body-scan practice and experiment with a comfortable seated or lying position.

title: Try a short seated movement session
description: Explore a few instructor-approved movements from a stable chair and choose a comfortable range.

title: Try a sport that terrifies you
description: Rock climbing, snowboarding, MMA. Do it badly. Keep going.

title: Try a supervised water-aerobics class
description: Join an instructor-led pool class that matches your confidence in water and any access needs.

title: Try curling at a supervised ice-rink taster
description: Learn delivery, sweeping and rink etiquette with a club before playing a short end.

title: Try fencing in a supervised beginner class
description: Learn the equipment checks, stop command and basic footwork before any coach-led partner exercise.

title: Try goalball at an inclusive sports session
description: Learn the court and listening rules with a coach before joining a short introductory game.

title: Try Kalamkari drawing on cloth with an artisan
description: Learn the handling of a traditional Kalamkari pen and complete a small cloth study with a practitioner.

title: Try polybat on an adapted table
description: Use a bat to send a ball along a side-walled table and learn a short rally game.

title: Try target archery at a supervised range
description: Learn the range commands and shoot your first group of arrows with an instructor.

title: Try wheelchair basketball at an introductory club session
description: Learn chair handling and basic ball skills using a club's suitable sports equipment.

title: Turn vegetable trimmings into stock and soup
description: Save suitable fresh trimmings, simmer a stock and use it in a complete meal.

title: Turn your next decade birthday into a mission
description: Will Smith skydived for his 50th. Make yours a declaration, not a dinner party.

title: Tuscany, Italy
description: Rolling hills, cypress trees, medieval villages, and wine made from grapes grown in sight of your table.

title: Uluru (Ayers Rock), Australia
description: The world's largest monolith changes colour from orange to purple to deep red as light moves across it. Sacred to the Anangu people.

title: Understand your own health at a deep level
description: Full bloodwork, genetics, a proper physical baseline. Know your body before it tells you something is wrong.

title: Vanuatu's volcanoes
description: Walk to the rim of Mount Yasur — an active volcano — and look into the crater. Legally accessible. Genuinely dangerous.

title: Venice before mass tourism erases it
description: A city built on water that shouldn't exist — and won't, at current rates. Go while it's still there.

title: Victoria Falls, Zambia/Zimbabwe
description: The world's largest waterfall by combined width and height. The mist is visible 50km away.

title: Visit a country you know nothing about
description: No guidebook research. Just go and figure it out.

title: Visit a repair cafe with a friend
description: Bring a suitable broken item, learn alongside a volunteer and share the repair process.

title: Visit all 50 US states
description: Alaska and Hawaii are the two that stall people. Most who finish do it in clusters across a decade.

title: Visit all seven wonders of the world
description: Petra, the Colosseum, Chichen Itza, Christ the Redeemer, the Great Wall, Machu Picchu, the Taj. Four continents, years of planning.

title: Visit every continent
description: Including Antarctica if you can. Each one has a climate, a culture, a geometry that's unlike anywhere else.

title: Visit Majuli's mask-making tradition with a local practitioner
description: Arrange a respectful visit to a participating satra or workshop and learn how masks connect to performance.

title: Visit the Taj Mahal at dawn
description: Gates open at sunrise and the marble runs pink to white within an hour. Closed Fridays for prayer.

title: Visit the temples of Angkor Wat, Cambodia
description: Over 400 square kilometres of ruins. Three days barely covers it, and the crowds thin sharply by mid-afternoon.

title: Volunteer abroad for at least a month
description: Pick an organisation that would exist without you. The skills they lack beat the enthusiasm they already have.

title: Volunteer at a hospital for a year
description: Mostly directions, tea, and sitting with patients whose families cannot get there. Weekly shifts, and nothing about it photographs well.

title: Volunteer for something you believe in
description: Not one afternoon — a sustained commitment where your absence would be noticed.

title: Wadi Rum, Jordan
description: The Valley of the Moon: red sandstone desert used as Mars in a dozen films. Spend a night in a Bedouin camp.

title: Walk 10,000 steps a day for a month
description: Roughly seven kilometres, or ninety minutes. The first week feels excessive; by the fourth it is just how you move.

title: Walk a labyrinth or pilgrimage slowly
description: Not a maze but a single winding path to the centre. Walk it slowly. The pace is the practice, not the destination.

title: Walk a long-distance trail over 100km
description: Four to seven days, a loaded pack, and weather you cannot control. The trail teaches you what your body can actually do.

title: Walk away from something comfortable but wrong
description: The job, the relationship, the city. Comfortable and right are different things.

title: Walk the Camino de Santiago (800km across Spain)
description: Roughly five weeks from the French border, and your feet set the schedule. Beds in albergues cost a few euros.

title: Watch a meteor shower from a dark sky location
description: Check the calendar for Perseids or Geminids. Drive an hour from city lights, bring a blanket, and stay until 2am.

title: Watch a rocket launch from an authorized public gallery
description: Plan around an official public viewing opportunity and learn the mission's purpose before launch day.

title: Watch a storm roll in from start to finish
description: Find a safe vantage point. Watch the clouds build, the wind shift, the rain arrive. Twenty minutes of weather as theatre.

title: Watch a sunrise and a sunset in the same day
description: Requires planning, not luck. Pick a day with a clear forecast, wake early, and find a west-facing spot for evening.

title: Watch the sunrise from a place that moved you
description: Not a beach resort — somewhere that earned the view. A summit, a desert, a cliffside you walked to.

title: Watch the sunrise from Machu Picchu, Peru
description: The first bus out of Aguas Calientes leaves before 5am and the queue starts earlier. Cloud often wins anyway.

title: Weave a miniature tapestry on cardboard
description: Make a small loom from packaging and weave a textile with changes in colour and texture.

title: White water raft a Class V river
description: Continuous rapids where a swim is genuinely dangerous. Guided trips exist, but you still paddle hard on command.

title: Win a competition you genuinely trained for
description: Not a participation trophy. Something you trained for, lost at, and came back to win. The losing is what makes it count.

title: Win something you genuinely competed for
description: A race, a pitch, a competition. Something where other people were trying to beat you.

title: Witness a geological or astronomical event
description: A total solar eclipse, an erupting volcano, the aurora. Scale that puts your problems in perspective.

title: Work or intern in another country
description: Even six months abroad rewires how you understand work and belonging.

title: Work through a celestial-navigation sight reduction
description: Use official astronomical data to calculate a practice altitude correction and compare it with a predicted altitude, entirely at a desk.

title: Write a book
description: Memoir, business, fiction. The discipline of writing a book is unlike anything else. The finished object is proof of self.

title: Write a book that changes someone's life
description: You will never know which reader it was. Write the thing you needed and could not find.

title: Write a forgiveness letter to yourself
description: You are the person you have been hardest on. Write the letter you would write to a friend who made your mistakes.

title: Write a letter to someone who changed your life
description: Send it. Don't wait for a funeral to say it.

title: Write a letter to someone who changed your life and send it
description: Do not wait for a funeral to say it. A handwritten letter carries weight no email can match.

title: Write a letter to someone you have not forgiven and then decide whether to send it
description: Write it first, decide later. The writing does the work whether or not the letter ever leaves your hands.

title: Write a letter to your future self and read it in 10 years
description: Seal it, date it, and put it somewhere you will find it. The person who opens it will be a stranger you once knew.

title: Write a letter to your younger self
description: What would you tell the person you were ten, twenty, thirty years ago? Write it honestly. The exercise is for you, not them.

title: Write a manifesto for how you want to live
description: Not resolutions but principles. One page, written in your own voice, that you can re-read when you forget who you decided to be.

title: Write and finish a novel
description: The finishing is the rare part. Eighty thousand words at five hundred a day is about six months.

title: Write and perform spoken word poetry
description: Written for the ear, so it only exists out loud. Most pieces change shape in the final rehearsal.

title: Write captions for ten unlabelled personal photos
description: Identify dates, people and context while you can, marking uncertain details rather than guessing.

title: Write down everything you know about your family history
description: Names, dates, places, stories. Start with your parents, then grandparents. The information dies with the people who hold it.

title: Write down your core values and check them against how you actually spend your time
description: List your values on one side. List your calendar and bank statements on the other. The gap is where the work is.

title: Write heartfelt letters to 10 people who changed your life
description: Handwritten, posted, no reply expected. Several will keep it in a drawer for the rest of their lives.

title: Write something and publish it
description: An essay, a story, a thread — something with your name on it, for public eyes.

title: Write the speech you would give at your own retirement
description: What would you say about the working years? Write it now, while you can still change what it would say.

title: Write the story of how you became who you are
description: Not a memoir for publication. The narrative of your own becoming, written for yourself. The act of writing changes the story.

title: Write your ethical will
description: Not your financial will — your values, lessons, and what you want passed down. The thing that matters.

title: Write your ethical will: values, lessons, what you want passed down
description: Not your financial will but your values. What you learned, what you got wrong, what you hope for the people who come after.

title: Write your memoir
description: Not everything that happened, only what it meant. Most first drafts are far too kind to the writer.

title: Write your obituary the way you would want it read
description: Not morbid but clarifying. What do you want to be remembered for? The gap between the obituary and your life is your to-do list.

title: Zanzibar, Tanzania
description: Stone Town's labyrinthine alleyways, spice plantations, and beaches that belong to a different planet than the mainland.

title: Zipline through a rainforest canopy
description: Thirty metres up on a steel cable, moving fast enough that the canopy blurs. Costa Rica built the template.
